entries.label: v1.9 maintenance: Jiangsu fast-response VPP and 2027 retail instance packs
items: Choice and rationale: two Jiangsu vertical slices cover the two main entity sides — the recommended load fast-response aggregator (solicitation-based VPP) and the backup 2027 retail company. The first answers "how much to declare at a call, how to deliver, how response is certified"; the second answers "how a 2027 package is priced, passed through and capped". Both packs need JSON and CSV edits only: about 30 minutes to fill in and under a minute to run.

VPP instance-layer schema: new skills/virtual-power-plant/instances/README.md defines the aggregation-side instance.json six blocks: meta; rules (fast-response product, baseline, spot background and settlement, each requiring grade + source); resources (replacing asset: control type, rated MW, adjustable ratio, availability, customer share, double-participation flag); policy (style profile); contracts (shortfall compensation and opex); and data_contract (baseline history, call and T+1 formats), plus a 30-minute workflow, validation checklist, acceptance criteria and data boundary.

Jiangsu fast-response pack: instances/jiangsu-fast-response-2026-11/ contains instance.json, run.py, make_demo.py, grade-D CSVs, a README and pitfalls. Rules follow 苏发改规发〔2026〕1号 (effective 2026-06-23 to 2029-07-13): power adjustment within 0.5 h; direct declaration cap 15 CNY/kWh with a 150% overshoot cap, self-controlled 10 CNY/kWh with 120%; "price priority, capacity priority" clearing; testing preferably in the evening peak 17:00–22:00 at ≥20% of the declared volume; no double participation in DR in the same period. Document No. 1 does not fix the baseline algorithm, so the pack applies the 2025 Jiangsu DR rules (5+3 class days, 15-minute points, drop days below 25% or above 200% of the mean) and marks it B/C pending; the 0.5 h event duration is a grade-D assumption.

Fast-response run chain and demo: validation → capability (rated × adjustable ratio × availability) → declaration (capability × style ratio, rounded down) → separate clearing for the two control types → T+1 response rate and cap → 11-bucket bridge → review. Grade-D demo: 30.66 MW direct / 10.80 MW self-controlled, declared 26.0 / 8.6 MW; plan net 45,881 CNY, scenario expectation 48,401, CVaR −2,000; T+1 actual 53,303, delta +7,423, residual 0; the self-controlled actual response rate is 125.6%, and the 0.48 MW above 120% is not paid.

Jiangsu 2027 retail pack: instances/jiangsu-retail-2027/ follows 苏电交易〔2026〕11号 (issued 2026-10-13, effective 2027-01-01): the fixed-price volume share, spot-linkage volume share and ratio sharing are abolished; P_retail = P_wholesale + P_float + ΣK×P_allocation, P_wholesale = (1−K1−K2)×P_MT + K1×P_DA + K2×P_RT; the reference price takes the pointwise maximum of the annual/monthly/intra-month/day-ahead/real-time layers and weights it by the user curve; the one-household-one-price cap is P_cap = P_ref + F×P_wholesale + P_allocation, where F is agreed by buyer and seller (5% in this pack), and a monthly average above the cap settles at the cap; green-power energy and environmental-value contracts are signed separately; the annual retail window runs 2026-10-16 to 2026-12-24, with at least one retail trade completed five working days before annual wholesale trading; time-of-use packages need peak ≥1.6× and valley ≤0.4× the flat weighted price.

Jiangsu 2027 run chain and demo: validation (rejecting F out of range, 2026 package types, reversed dates and wrong units) → wholesale/reference prices → four customer-segment pass-through and per-household caps → five scenarios plus four stress sets → 6-bucket bridge → review. Grade-D demo: 1,972.7 MWh, P_MT 401.00, wholesale average 395.01, reference 428.52, retail 456.48, average cap 454.74 CNY/MWh, weighted clip 1.75, 4/4 segments capped; plan 89,692, expected 92,043, CVaR10 89,692, actual 93,280, delta +3,588, residual 0. Only the ×1.0 stress case clips while ×0.8/×1.2/×1.5 do not: the reference price rises almost 1:1 with spot while the wholesale price is only about 30% linked, which is structural for full pass-through.

Self-test and verification: the VPP selftest.py gains section E instance assertions and asymmetric-baseline cases (150 assertions); the retail selftest.py gains section J (configuration, fingerprint 3cfa9f5ae1b1, rejection of six invalid configurations, exact pricing/scenario/stress/bridge numbers and complete outputs); all nine Python self-tests pass.

entries.label: v1.9 maintenance: Guangdong retail instance pack
items: Why and where it sits: the Shandong pack proved the spot loop from configuration to bidding, settlement and review, but a retailer's problem is not a charge/discharge curve; it is package pricing, procurement matching, deviation and guarantees. The second slice is a Guangdong retail company: one province, one entity, JSON and CSV only, about 30 minutes to fill in and under a minute to run.

Instance-layer schema: new skills/retail-electricity-risk/instances/README.md defines the retail instance.json six blocks: meta (identity, rule version, data cutoff, energy-only scope), rules (spot price zone, retail market, deviation, guarantee, settlement, each requiring grade + source), portfolio (replacing the spot pack's asset: customer shares, fixed/linked parameters, forecast error, opex, deviation contract, guarantee), policy (style profile), contracts (medium-term cover locked to forecast load) and data_contract (D-1/T+1 fields and scenario weights), plus a 30-minute workflow, validation checklist, acceptance criteria and data boundary.

Guangdong pack: instances/guangdong-retail-2026-11/ contains instance.json, run.py, make_demo.py, synthetic D-1/T+1 CSVs, a pack README and ten province-specific pitfalls. Rule values carry sources: Southern regional Guangdong price zone with a −50 declaration floor and −50 to 1,800 CNY/MWh clearing band (A/B); the old pilot 0–1,000 / 70–1,500 is kept as a historical field; 15-minute / 96 points; 2026H1 retail average 407.4 and per-MWh margin 3.9 are background only; the ±3%/±5% deviation claim is grade C and unverified, so the pack computes contracted terms instead; the current guarantee follows 1595, while the 2026-09-04 draft is marked "not effective" and fails validation if set effective; settlement follows 976 with 5/8/10 working days and a 15-day objection window.

Run chain: run.py validates configuration and data, builds a pointwise weighted-quantile reference price from five scenarios, computes W = 75%×400 + 25%×S_ref, builds full cost (wholesale + expected deviation + opex + guarantee funding + fixed + risk buffer + target margin), recommends fixed prices and linked adders with break-even spot prices, evaluates five scenario margins, CVaR10 and spot/sigma stress, splits the T+1 variance into nine buckets (retail volume/price, spot volume/price/cross, contract, deviation assessment, opex, guarantee funding) and writes the review; the style fingerprint goes into summary.json and the review.

Worked example (synthetic grade D): trading day 2026-11-18, 2,880 MWh portfolio, reference price 375.67 CNY/MWh, weighted procurement 393.92, current retail price 414.43, recommended full cost 418.14, weighted gap +3.71; plan margin CNY 37,070, scenario expected 26,063, CVaR10 −28,354, net spot exposure 309.6 MWh, break-even rise +31.9%; actual 19,898, delta −17,172, residual −1.75e-10. Industrial fixed 405 is below its 418.60 full cost while the data centre at 428 is above 414.66, so the weighted gap of only 3.71 means the data centre is cross-subsidising the industrial customer; the review must show the segments separately.

Self-test and verification: tools/selftest.py gains section I with instance assertions: valid configuration, 96 points / 15 minutes, stable style fingerprint, rejection of missing grades, shares not summing to one, unknown packages and wrong units, exact locking of pricing, scenario and bridge numbers, CVaR ≤ expected, nine buckets summing to the delta, and all seven output files present; all nine Python self-tests pass.

Boundaries: no new knowledge module, skill or section (still 101 / 13 / 9); energy-only, with network tariffs, surcharges, capacity/basic charges, green premiums, bad debt, churn and taxes excluded; v1 supports fixed and market_linked only, leaving multi-contract and time-of-use contracts to a later version; demo data is synthetic grade D and real customer/contract/metering data stays local; out/ directories are now git-ignored.

Synchronised: Chinese and English skills gain §12.1 with commands and baseline numbers; both READMEs add the Guangdong retail instance pack to the skill table; the maintenance checklist gains a retail instance-layer note, linked-module update and ledger row; the spot instance README and Shandong pack README cross-link the retail pack; skill pages and TXT downloads are rebuilt.

Verification: build, --check, matrix --check, consistency, maintenance ledger, policy links, git diff --check and all nine Python self-tests pass; 42,293 body lines unchanged (no knowledge-module edits), 3,651 sections, 1,402 tables and 273 code/diagram blocks unchanged, and the search index remains 3,593,740 bytes.

entries.label: v1.9 maintenance: Shandong storage instance pack and desk configuration layer
items: Why and where it sits: the knowledge base is good for education and onboarding but cannot supply a trading edge; the engine layer already has methods, examples and desk tools, but lacked a "one province, one entity, fill in the config and run" instance layer. The first vertical slice is a Shandong standalone storage asset, proving the full loop from configuration to bidding, settlement and review rather than writing another generic strategy.

Instance-layer schema: new skills/spot-bidding-quant/instances/README.md defines six instance.json blocks: meta (identity, rule version, data cutoff, scope), rules (spot limits, settlement, capacity compensation, storage participation, negative prices, VPP thresholds, each requiring grade + source), asset (power, energy, SOC, RTE, degradation, effective capacity), policy (a style profile kept separate from asset parameters), contracts (CfD) and data_contract (D-1/T+1 fields, scenario weights, release cutoff). It also documents a 30-minute fill-in workflow, validation checklist, acceptance criteria, data-locality boundary and steps for a second instance.

Shandong pack: instances/shandong-storage-2026-11/ contains instance.json, run.py, make_demo.py, synthetic D-1/T+1 CSVs, a pack README and ten province-specific pitfalls. Rule values carry sources: current declaration limits −80 to 1,300 and clearing limits −100 to 1,500 CNY/MWh (grade B/C); the 2026-08-28 −120/−140 draft is kept in a separate field marked "not effective"; standalone storage bids quantity and price from 2026-01-01 (A/B); capacity compensation is "effective capacity × compensation standard × supply-demand coefficient" (A), with the standard and coefficient left null and shown as pending rather than estimated; the 100 MW / 200 MWh / 180 MWh usable / 0.86 RTE asset is a grade-D placeholder.

Run chain: run.py validates the configuration and data, runs the SOC-aware DP in ems-dispatch/tools/dispatch.py once per scenario, synthesises declared quantities and reference prices at the style quantiles, applies discharge markup and charge markdown inside the provincial limits, enforces the minimum spread and cycle cap, repairs SOC, evaluates price-taker clearing and CVaR10, builds the T+1 bridge and writes the review. The SHA-1 prefix of the policy block is written into the review, so style changes need no code change.

Tool extension: tools/desk.py gains storage_bridge, separating discharge and charge quantity, price and cross terms (six buckets) from degradation, contract, capacity, penalty and allocation (five buckets), with an exact identity gap of zero. The CfD overlay uses Qc·(Pc − P), algebraically identical to the physical convention Qc·Pc + (Q − Qc)·P.

Worked example (synthetic grade D): trading day 2026-11-18; declared discharge 271.3 MWh, charge 315.4 MWh, 1.47 cycles; scenario expected net margin CNY 65,196, CVaR10 CNY −23,135 (low-price scenarios charge but do not discharge, the cost of an aggressive spike markup, not an arithmetic error); the bridge moves planned 124,506 to actual 107,926 (−16,579), identity gap 0.00e+00; the largest bucket is discharge quantity −24,085, with the top five slots at 20:45–21:45 (planned 96 MW, actual 0).

Pitfalls: ten items — draft treated as current, missing negative signs on the floor, capacity compensation merged into energy spread, 447.41/416.69 settlement averages used as spot prices, three electricity-volume calibres mixed, 59 registered entities versus 54 stations in the spot market versus 10.045 GW installed, VPP ≥1 MW/≥2 h applied to standalone storage, a single price curve without scenarios, hourly curves interpolated to 96 points, and quantity-price bidding used on one side only; plus two notes: the 136 mechanism price is not for storage, and the 2024-06-17 spot launch is not the 2026-01-01 new rules.

Boundaries: no new knowledge module, skill or section (still 101 modules / 13 sections / 9 skills); v1 covers spot energy plus a capacity-compensation placeholder and CfD only, with ancillary services, medium-term curve decomposition and leasing out of scope; demo data is synthetic grade D and real asset/contract/metering data stays local; the tool does not route orders or replace exchange settlement.

Synchronised: Chinese and English skills gain §13.6, two formula-map rows and an instance-CSV note in §16.3; both READMEs add the Shandong instance pack to the skill table; the maintenance checklist gains an instance-layer note and a ledger row; desk.py self-tests gain exact assertions for all 11 storage buckets and a full instance run (configuration validation, cycle cap, CVaR ≤ expected, bridge gap < 1e-6).

Verification: build, --check, matrix --check, consistency, maintenance ledger, policy links, git diff --check and all nine Python self-tests pass; 42,293 body lines unchanged (no knowledge-module edits), 3,651 sections, 1,402 tables and the 3,593,740-byte search index unchanged.

entries.label: v1.9 maintenance: desk layer in the spot-bidding skill
items: Why and where it sits: the institutional and rules layer is already covered by the electricity-trading skill, so spot-bidding-quant gains a §13 desk layer that closes four gaps between a model and a trading desk: §13.1 the trading day (five clocks and nine decision points, each with data cutoff, decision, output and failure mode; three disciplines: no backfilling after a cutoff, every manual override logged, and submission/clearing/settlement aligned on one ID); §13.2 bid curves under uncertainty (scenario sets, expected profit versus CVaR frontier, contract coverage and markup comparison, with the price-taker/pivotal boundary made explicit); §13.3 settlement disputes and implicit losses (four-term bridge plus seven buckets, four kinds of implicit cost, a five-step dispute process and evidence pack); §13.4 a one-province one-period public-data backtest (L1/L2/L3 capability limits, minimum data contract, release-time leakage control, eight deliverables).

Key examples (synthetic grade D): a 350 MW unit with CNY 20,000/day fixed cost gives expected profit of 17,835 / 14,585 / 11,335 CNY/day at 0/100/200 MW contract coverage, with CVaR10 of -20,000 / -7,200 / -400 CNY/day; all three sit on the non-dominated frontier. The cost curve dominates a 5%/10% markup (14,585 versus 14,465; mean dispatch 236.5 versus 224.5 MW), putting "markup is not free revenue" on the desk. The settlement case moves planned profit 28,000 to actual 34,300, a +6,300 delta, with buckets -3,200/+4,000/+9,600/+600/-2,200/-2,000/-500 and an identity gap of zero; implicit cost is 6,000 opportunity plus 2,000 assessment = 8,000, and a 1,000 CNY threshold yields a five-item dispute packet.

Tools and self-tests: new zero-dependency tools/desk.py (nine-step clock, curve dispatch, weighted CVaR, scenario metrics, non-dominated frontier, settlement bridge, implicit cost, dispute packet, and a schema/duplicate/96-slot/order check for public data); tools/selftest.py gains desk assertions that lock every number above and injects a duplicate row and a missing row to prove the data gate rejects both (5,760 rows / 60 days / 96 slots pass).

Docs and boundaries: Chinese and English skills expand together; former chapters 13-15 become 14-16; the formula map gains eight desk.* rows, the glossary gains desk layer / data cutoff / risk frontier / settlement bridge / implicit loss / public-data backtest, and §16.3 and §16.5 are updated. The engineering module §1.3 and §13, the index note §5 and both READMEs gain pointers without duplicating the engineering architecture. No new knowledge module, skill or section (still 101 modules / 13 sections / 9 skills); the desk layer does no market feed, order routing or position keeping and does not replace exchange settlement, a risk committee or legal advice.

Watch list: public-data disclosure fields, release timing and revision policy join the quarterly review; the 2026 spot rules (proposed 2027-01-01), secondary caps and the scope of quantity-only renewable bidding are unchanged.

Verification: build, --check, matrix --check, consistency, maintenance ledger, policy links, git diff --check and all nine Python self-tests pass; 42,293 body lines (+3), 3,651 sections, 1,402 tables and a 3,593,740-byte search index.

entries.label: v1.9 maintenance: trading-integration modes and interface watch in the storage EMS note
items: Section 1.7 gains an integration dimension: the six business-form table now carries a mode column (position-holding / price-taking / instruction-following / non-market objective), and a new §1.7.1 defines four trading-integration modes by "who holds the position and where the dispatch instruction comes from", with criteria, typical forms, EMS duties and integration focus. It states that overseas markets are a different interface for the same modes, not a fifth mode (ERCOT and Australia's NEM co-optimise energy and ancillary services), gives three screening questions (independent market registration, source of dispatch instructions, market revenue share of gross margin), and requires capacity partitioning into self-use / reserve / tradable when one asset sits in several modes, with the same capacity never sold twice (the two checks in §4.14). Two easily missed interfaces are added: the internal market of parks and direct green-power connections, and the aggregation layer of VPPs.

Forward interface watch: new §1.10, six changes that will reshape the interface over the next 12-24 months (finer settlement granularity, joint energy and ancillary clearing, distributed and household market entry / VPP aggregation, direct green-power connection and internal settlement, persistent negative prices, finer capacity-payment and performance tests), each with its EMS impact, observable indicator and a 2027-06 review date. All are grade B/C judgements and are refreshed within one month of a rule change.

Cross-references: microgrid EMS §4.12 gains a pointer to the modes and capacity partitioning; SCADA §9.3 now states that SCADA is not a trading system and only passes capability envelopes and execution feedback; the index and calibre note adds the EMS/trading boundary in section 5. No new module, skill or section (still 101 modules / 13 sections / 9 skills).

Calibre and scope: the four modes are a synthesis, not an official classification; spot-market coverage cites the provincial matrix (11 formal / 4 regional formal / 14 trial / 4 not running, as of 2026-11-08); the six forward items are not a policy timetable.

items: Priority 3 delivered: a new §2.1.1 Structural load: the baseload itself is changing under 气象与电力交易-2026-11.md §2.1. items: New fuel module: knowledge/燃料与电力交易-2026-11.md (m-cross-fuel, eighth cross-cutting note, 243 lines). Weather supplies quantity, fuel supplies price, the grid supplies deliverability. Eight sections cover China's dual-track thermal-coal contracts, CNY/t to CNY/MWh conversion, bid curves and the capacity-payment boundary, dark/spark/clean spreads, the coal-to-gas switching carbon price, inventory and contract risk, synthetic grade-D examples and verification entry points.

Key calibres: the 2026 5,500 kcal long-term contract uses a 675 CNY/t base inside a 570-770 band with a 0.5 slope (675 + (four-index mean - 675)/2); coal producers must contract >=75% of their own output and generators >=80% of demand, with monthly >=80% and quarterly/annual >=90% fulfillment; September 2026 contract price ~704 CNY/t versus ~989 CNY/t spot; six major utilities' cover fell from 17.2 to 15.2 days. The base price and formula come from listed-company disclosures and trade press, not an NDRC original; the module grades them B/C and lists the original document as unverified.

Congestion cross-reference: knowledge/省间与跨区交易-2026-11.md §5.2 was corrected against the official 734-doc interim scheme and the NDRC June press conference: priority-plan capacity first, Fujian/Guangdong priority use (retaining <=50%), residual capacity released monthly; spot transmission rights are allocated automatically, not auctioned; the price band is 25.6-100 CNY/MW·h (per MW per hour); the first trade drew 113 entities for 21.16 GWh (16.07 GWh green). Unverified trade-press claims were withdrawn. New §5.5 compares four congestion-management methods across China/Europe/North America and §5.6 covers dynamic ATC, market power and weather x congestion superposition; the 734 pilot now appears in 更新清单.md §3.2 as a rolling watch item.

Two zero-dependency tools: electricity-trading-expert/tools/fuel.py and spot-bidding-quant/tools/network.py. entries.label: v1.9 maintenance: weather and power trading cross-cutting note
items: New module: knowledge/气象与电力交易-2026-11.md (m-cross-weather, seventh cross-cutting note, 291 lines). Weather does not set prices directly: it enters clearing through four mediators — load, wind/solar output, hydro inflow and equipment availability. Eight sections cover NWP and reanalysis sourcing, four conversion chains, net load and the 96-point price shape, error attribution and compliance, extreme weather and security of supply, weather-risk contracts, synthetic grade-D examples, and verification entry points.

Key facts: in summer 2026 each 1 C rise in national mean temperature lifted demand by 40-50 GW, with cooling load near 30% nationally and above 40% in some provinces (B, NEA / CEC); power-forecast duties cover 240 h / 72 h / 15 min-4 h at 15-minute resolution, 100% reporting rates and province-specific accuracy thresholds (A, regulator rules); the 2025 Northwest supplement switches the deviation baseline to available power; CME degree-day futures use 20 index points at USD 20 per point, versus EUR 20 in Europe and JPY 2,500 for Tokyo CAT (A/B). Every figure carries date, calibre and grade; drafts are flagged and unverified items say so.

Zero-dependency tool: skills/spot-bidding-quant/tools/weather.py (degree days, wind power curve and air-density correction, cell temperature and PV output, ensemble quantiles, newsvendor bid quantity, weather-index payout and basis gap, lagged runoff index). Five grade-D examples are locked to new assertions in selftest.py; CI still runs nine self-tests with no workflow change.

Shape: no 14th section and no tenth skill — weather is a horizontal input, forecasting methodology already belongs to spot-bidding-quant §3-§5 and the quantitative bidding module §4, so the new note only adds pointers. Long-term climate change is deliberately kept separate.

items: Two executable skill toolkits (P1): electricity-trading-expert and virtual-power-plant had no tools/ directory, breaking the repo rule that every worked example must be runnable. The new tooling caught a typo in the prose: §8.4 of the VPP note listed "about 16.3%" IRR for the CAPEX +20% case, inconsistent with its own NPV 4.568m and 5.28-year payback. Rebuilt from §8.3 parameters it is 13.71%; the table now reads "about 13.7%" with a correction note, and selftest.py locks the value. The other four cases (18.0 / 7.4 / 13.9 / 17.0%) all reconcile.

items: New cross-cutting module: modules 62→63, body lines 27,423→27,818, Markdown files 85→86 (63 knowledge modules + 18 skill files + 5 repository-level documents). New ten-market same-caliber snapshot and decision calendar (m-cross-snapshot, sixth cross module, 349 lines including frontmatter).

Same-caliber snapshot: ten markets × seven columns (installed capacity, storage stock/pipeline, 2025–2026 average price, negative-price hours, capture rate, interconnection queue and de-rating factor), each cell with value/grade/time; states explicitly that no market module carries both national total installed capacity and annual day-ahead average price, and that storage stock, permitted, auction and pipeline figures are not interchangeable; includes a gap list and next-round data priorities.

Interconnection-queue comparison: UK ~750 GW → 200–250 GW (C), Italy ~277 GW storage applications (B), Spain ~37.37 GW (C), Netherlands ~15,000 businesses and ~9 GW ATR85 non-firm (B/C), PJM 715 projects/201.5 GW with ~40-month studies (A), ERCOT ~474 GW (C); reads four governance models (TMO4+, RDL 7/2026 flexible access, ATR85, Batch Zero).

Event calendar: 2026Q4–2027 in three blocks, including Italy MACSE round 2 on 2026-11-24 (16 GWh), Netherlands SDE++ closing 2026-11-26, Germany's second 4.5 GW capacity auction on 2026-12-29, the UK LDES final decision (autumn 2026), Spain's first capacity auction (late 2026–2027), Germany's AgNes final decision 2027-01-01, the end of Dutch net metering 2027-01-01, and Germany's ~2 GW storage ≥10 h auction in 2027; items without a confirmed date are marked "to be verified".

China-entry checklist: ten markets × six gates (local entity, tax, FDI review, certification/grid code, balancing responsibility, credit/insurance), with country notes, six common gates and ten market-specific remarks.

Grade-C verification page: 20 grade-C figures (Belgian CRM unit, Poland's 13% de-rating, Italy's 54% cap, the Dutch 15,000 queue, Spanish negative-price/permitted/application figures, the UK queue, Poland's 685 MW and negative price, Belgian Y-4, Japan's 24,880 applications and JEPX price, ERCOT/PJM/CAISO, and others), each with its module location, why it cannot be used directly, a verification entry and a P0/P1/P2 priority; plus a four-step verification method.

Ten pointers: the Australia, Germany, UK, Italy, Spain, Netherlands, Poland, Belgium/Nordics, US and Japan modules each gain a cross-reference in their "division of labour" section pointing to §1–§2, §4 and §5 of the new module, without duplicating the tables.

Indexes and skills: INDEX_EN gains a module row, six key-figure rows and open item #36; the electricity-trading skill (both languages, §7A.13) and the storage skill (both languages, §15.3) each gain a snapshot entry.

Docs and counts: README / README_EN move to 63 modules / 27,818 body lines / 12 sections / 63 knowledge pages; 更新清单 moves its inventory to 63 Markdown files (62 Chinese modules + 1 English index), P1 from 27 to 28 items, and records this round.

Sources and links: verification entries are mostly official domains as code text; stable official pages (CREG, URE, PSE, GME, OMIE, REE, ACM, NESO, Ofgem, OCCTO, JEPX, ERCOT, PJM, CAISO, BNetzA, ENTSO-E) are clickable; Elia, Terna, AEMO and AEMC returned 403 to automated access and are kept as code text with the status noted.

Checks: 63 knowledge pages + 18 skill pages + 18 TXT files were rebuilt (27,818 body lines, 2,381 sections, 913 tables, 267 code/diagram blocks); --check and the consistency check pass, with the consistency check reading 86 Markdown files. Version remains v1.9; nothing is committed or pushed.

Pending-item verification (2026-11-11): the Nordic bidding-zone review now resolves to the Swedish government press release of 2026-05-29 — Svenska kraftnät's mandate is extended, with a structural-congestion and optimal-zone report due 2027-01-29; the Government decides on any change (grade A for the process, outcome pending), mirrored in the Nordics module §3.1, snapshot §3.2 and source table. Japan's LTDA round 4 now cites OCCTO's 2026-10-09 announcement of the registration and bidding schedule (grade A); the expected decarbonised-power volume is ~6 GW (grade C, METI 2026-05-13 material), while the price cap and results remain pending, mirrored in the Japan module §5.2, the observation list and the capacity/storage calendars. The 20 grade-C work orders in §5 remain 20, with priorities unchanged; no figure was upgraded.

Landing refinements: the Nordics module §3.1 gains a bidding-zone review timeline and investment implications (mandate 2026-05-29, report 2027-01-29, government decision, implementation; a report is not a decision; three sensitivities for zone spreads, EPAD hedging and siting; model the current 12 zones until the outcome is known). The Japan module §5.2 gains a round-4 progress table (schedule published 2026-10-09; registration/bidding and cap to be verified; results expected in 2027) and corrects the "36% award rate" to the lithium-ion caliber (551/1,525 MW), adding the overall ~67%, all-battery ~46% and lithium 36% rates plus a warning not to extrapolate round-3 clearing prices. The snapshot §3.2 gains a reading note that both process milestones are not outcomes.

Review fixes: cross-checked against the ten source modules; Spain now shows only a solar capture price of ~€33.95/MWh, down ~19.7% year on year (previously mislabelled as "vs baseload"); the Dutch queue is labelled all business types; Italy's pipeline is "advanced-permit projects"; Belgium/Nordics negative prices are year-on-year; Japan's demand figure is FY2026; Poland's OZE auction is "scheduled" rather than "held"; Italy's FER X is 37.15 GW total with a 10 GW solar quota; Italy's 54% and Germany's 4.5 GW auction are treated as grade C in both the table and the review page; PJM's 2028/29 $325, 2027/28 $333.44 and 2026/27 $329.17 are corrected in the English index.

entries.label: v1.9 maintenance: cross-cutting section and five cross-market modules
items: New cross-cutting section: sections 11→12, modules 57→62, body lines 24,538→27,423, Markdown files 80→85 (62 knowledge modules + 18 skill files + 5 repository-level documents). The cross section is numbered 07 / CROSS, placed after intl and before price, with an olive/bronze palette; the five modules are overseas grid connection and compliance, capacity mechanisms, ancillary services and balancing markets, storage revenue modelling and data sources, and cross-border PPAs.

Overseas grid connection and compliance: new overseas grid connection and compliance handbook (m-cross-grid, first cross module, 741 body lines). Covers the EU RfG/EN 50549 layer versus national implementation, connection points in ten markets (VDE-AR-N 4110/4120/4130, G99/G100, CEI 0-21/0-16, NTS/RD 647/2020, Netcode, Poland), the certification map (IEC 62933, UL 9540/9540A, NFPA 855, CEI 0-16), fire review, NIS2 cybersecurity, the EU Battery Regulation and battery passport (mandatory 2027-02-18, 71 data points), NZIA non-price criteria, and FDI screening (CFIUS/FEFTA/FIRB/NSIA); plus a compliance timeline, investment checklist and a grade-D example.

Capacity mechanism comparison: new capacity mechanism comparison (m-cross-capacity, second cross module, 634 body lines). Separates capacity annuities, long-term capacity auctions, two-way CfDs/revenue underwriting, strategic reserves and energy-only + scarcity pricing, then normalises units ($/MW-day × 365 ÷ 1000 = $/kW-yr; €/MWh-yr × duration ÷ 1000 = €/kW-yr); covers UK CM, Italy CM+MACSE, Spain TED/966/2026, Poland rynek mocy, Belgium CRM, Swedish/Finnish strategic reserves, Germany StromVKG, Australia CIS and PJM/Japan, distinguishes nameplate, connection, de-rated, ELCC and NQC capacity, and adds storage capacity-revenue modelling plus a 10-question investment checklist.

Ancillary services and balancing markets: new ancillary services and balancing market comparison (m-cross-ancillary, third cross module, 486 body lines). Organised by six function families (inertia/fast frequency response, frequency restoration, reserve/replacement, ramping, voltage/reactive power, black start); covers European FCR/aFRR/mFRR and PICASSO/MARI/TERRE access, UK BM and DC/DM/DR products, about ten Australian FCAS products, ERCOT/PJM/CAISO ancillary services, Italian MSD/MB, Nordic mFRR EAM and Japanese EPRX five products plus combined; storage eligibility, SOC and opportunity cost are treated separately, with three grade-D examples.

Storage revenue modelling and data sources: new storage revenue modelling and data sources (m-cross-revenue, fourth cross module, 479 body lines). Provides data access points and APIs for ENTSO-E, NEMWEB, Elexon BMRS, GME, OMIE, PSE, Nord Pool and the US/Japanese markets; works through 5/15/30-minute granularity, UTC versus local time, DST, RTE, cycle/calendar/high-frequency degradation, de-rating, capture price and spread capture, revenue-stacking conflicts and backtest bias; includes LCOS and 15-year cash-flow examples (grade D).

Cross-border PPAs, certificates and tolling: new cross-border PPAs, certificates and tolling (m-cross-ppa, fifth cross module, 511 body lines). Covers eight contract structures (merchant, pay-as-produced, baseload, financial/virtual PPA, collar/floor/cap, proxy revenue swap, tolling, CfD/CIS), effective price and capture rate, six certificate systems (EU GO, UK REGO, US REC, Australian LGC, Japanese NFC, China GEC) and a "no mutual recognition by default" matrix; AIB in 2026-11 reports 42 members + 6 observers from 36 countries, EU GOs are valid for 12 months from production, and EEX French June 2026 GO auctions cleared at regional weighted averages of €1.73–1.85/MWh for about 4.05 TWh; also covers CfD/CIS stacking, merchant tails, 12 tolling clauses and 24/7 hourly matching, with five grade-D examples.

Home page and atlas: the knowledge map gains a sixth layer, "X cross-cutting topics", with five chips, a cross palette and section card; the home-page count becomes 62 modules / 12 sections, and the atlas and filters are updated; the coverage string in scripts/knowledge.config.mjs includes cross-cutting topics.

Indexes and skills: INDEX_EN gains five module rows, 15 cross-cutting key-figure rows and open items #31–#35 (grid compliance, capacity mechanisms, ancillary services, storage revenue data, cross-border PPAs/certificates); the electricity-trading skill (both languages) adds §7A.13 cross-cutting topics, and the storage skill (both languages) adds five maintenance entries to §15.3, noting that single-market modules should confirm local rules before cross-market comparison.

Docs and counts: README / README_EN move to 62 modules / 27,423 body lines / 12 sections / 62 knowledge pages and add cross-cutting descriptions; 更新清单 moves its inventory to 62 Markdown files (61 Chinese modules + 1 English index), P1 from 22 to 27 items with five new review rows, and records this round.

Sources and links: AIB, EEX French GO auctions, Ofgem REGO, CER, JEPX, EPA Green Power, GHG Protocol, GOV.UK and the NDRC 2023/2025 GEC documents returned 200; EUR-Lex (RED II) returned 202 (anti-bot challenge), while GSE and DCCEEW were restricted to automated access and are shown as code text with the status noted; volatile figures such as auction results, GO prices and de-rating factors carry a grade and a date.

Checks: 62 knowledge pages + 18 skill pages + 18 TXT files were rebuilt (27,423 body lines, 2,353 sections, 899 tables, 265 code/diagram blocks); --check and the consistency check pass, with the consistency check reading 85 Markdown files. Version remains v1.9; nothing is committed or pushed.

entries.label: v1.9 maintenance: US and Japan modules added; storage module expanded to ten markets
items: Two new overseas modules: modules 55→57, body lines 23,406→24,538, Markdown files 78→80 (57 knowledge modules + 18 skill files + 5 repository-level documents). The intl order is Australia NEM (1), Germany (2), UK (3), Italy (4), Spain (5), Netherlands (6), Poland (7), Belgium/Nordics (8), United States (9), Japan (10), overseas storage business (11); scripts/knowledge.config.mjs moves its section description and coverage to ten markets.

US electricity market: new US electricity market (m-intl-us, ninth intl module, 487 body lines). Covers ERCOT energy-only + ORDC (5-minute SCED, 15-minute settlement, HCAP/LCAP $5,000/$2,000 per MWh, RTC+B from 2025-12-05), PJM's capacity market (2028/29 BRA at the $325/MW-day cap, 152.1 GW cleared, 6.8 GW gap, 14.7% reserve margin, about 525 MW of new effective capacity, 4-hour battery ELCC around 50%), CAISO day-ahead + 15-minute FMM + 5-minute RTD, RA slice-of-day, EDAM from 2026-05-01 and >21 GW of storage; interconnection queues (PJM 715 projects/201.5 GW, about 40 months; CAISO about 197 GW), ITC 30% + 10% domestic content + 10% energy community, FEOC for construction after 2025-12-31, Section 301 at 25% from 2026-01-01, UL 9540/NFPA 855; Chinese entry paths, ten pitfalls and a China–US comparison, with three synthetic worked examples (grade D).

Japan electricity market: new Japan electricity market (m-intl-jp, tenth intl module, 453 body lines). Covers ten supply areas, JEPX day-ahead with 48 half-hour products (10:00 gate, ¥0.01/kWh floor, no negative prices), 30-minute imbalance (C value ¥300 and D value ¥50/kWh from 2026-10-01, grade C), the capacity market (four years ahead, single price, one-year contracts; FY2028 ¥11,134/kW, FY2029 ¥13,303/kW), EPRX with five products plus combined (cap ¥10.00/ΔkW·30min from 2026-09-01), LTDA (20 years, pay-as-bid, about 90% clawback, ≥6 hours from round 3, 1,251 MW/19 battery projects), FIT/FIP, non-fossil certificates, SII grants, 24,880 connection-study applications in FY2025 and the 2026-08-01 per-applicant caps, and FEFTA review; Chinese entry paths, ten pitfalls and a China–Japan comparison, with three synthetic worked examples (grade D).

Storage module expanded to ten markets: Overseas storage business: large-scale and C&I storage in ten markets (m-intl-storage, eleventh intl module) adds sections for the three US markets and Japan (six subsections each, one structure), expands the large-scale comparison to thirteen rows and the C&I comparison to ten rows, grows the pitfall list to 16, and adds China–US and China–Japan comparison tables plus 2026–2027 watch items; the body grows from 1,181 to 1,395 lines.

Home page and atlas: the secondary knowledge map gains chips for the US and Japanese markets; atlas 08 becomes "Australia / Germany / UK / Italy / Spain / Netherlands / Poland / Belgium–Nordics / US / Japan market and storage design comparison", the flow moves to 10 steps (new .market-flow.ten, five columns over two rows on desktop, two columns at ≤960px and one at ≤620px), mini cards add US capacity/ELCC/ERCOT and Japan capacity/LTDA, the fact row becomes 5 NEM regions / 7 Italian zones / 2 Iberian zones / 12 Nordic zones / 10 overseas modules, and the caption covers ten markets.

Skills: the electricity-trading skill (both languages) moves §7A from eight to ten markets — new "7A.1c United States and Japan cards", new "US three markets: five must-knows" (7A.9b) and "Japan: five must-knows" (7A.9c), the same-question table becomes ten-way with a US/Japan table, answering discipline (7A.11) adds USD/JPY, CT/ET/PT/JST, FERC/ISO/RTO and the Japanese Electricity Business Act hierarchy, and the reading path (7A.12) adds both modules. The storage skill (both languages) mirrors §14A to ten markets with 14A.1c cards, 14A.9b US points, 14A.9c Japan points, a ten-way 14A.10 comparison and 14A.11 discipline; maintenance entries and quarterly review add both modules.

Indexes and docs: INDEX_EN adds US and Japan module rows and 11 overseas key-figure rows, plus open items #29 (US) and #30 (Japan); README / README_EN move to 57 modules / 24,538 body lines / 57 knowledge pages and add the US and Japan to descriptions and entry tables; 更新清单 moves its inventory to 57 Markdown files (56 Chinese modules + 1 English index), P1 from 20 to 22 items, and updates the skill-linkage and generated-artifact counts.

Sources and links: ERCOT, PJM, CAISO, EIA, IRS, UL, NFPA, gov.texas.gov, JEPX, OCCTO (including capacity-market and tender pages) and EPRX returned 200; FERC, METI and the Agency for Natural Resources and Energy returned 403 and are shown as code text with the status noted; treasury.gov, puct.texas.gov, energy.ca.gov and mof.go.jp returned 000 and are not clickable. Volatile figures such as the PJM BRA, ERCOT battery capacity and Japanese capacity-market/LTDA results carry a grade and a date.

Checks: 57 knowledge pages + 18 skill pages + 18 TXT files were rebuilt (24,538 body lines, 2,120 sections, 798 tables, 220 code/diagram blocks); --check and the consistency check pass, with the consistency check reading 80 Markdown files. Version remains v1.9; nothing is committed or pushed.

UK: the balancing-mechanism gate-closure wording changed from "before the half-hourly delivery period" to "one hour before the start of the delivery period", mirrored in the Chinese and English skills; all other key figures (NESO 2024-10-01, both EPEX GB auction gates, T-4/T-1 results, 7.5 GW of grid-scale batteries, LDES 7,645 MW) checked out.

Poland electricity market: new Poland module (m-intl-pl, seventh in intl, 688 body lines). Covers the single bidding zone and TGE RDN/RDB, PSE dispatch, URE regulation, the 15-minute MTU since 2025-10-01 and 15-minute imbalance; the rynek mocy capacity market (2030 delivery year: Polish price PLN 465.02/kW·yr, synchronous profile 78.00, Lithuania 418.00, Sweden 444.67; obligation 6,887.639 MW; foreign awards 992 MW; multi-year contracts 3,879.177 MW; cumulative 2021–2030 21,785.155 MW; ended in round 2; 2029 delivery year PLN 264.9/kW·yr, 245 units, cumulative 20.36 GW); battery de-rating around 13% and about 685 MW awarded for 2030 (grade C); OZE auctions with 15-year CfDs (2025 PV PLN 216.90–329.68/MWh and wind PLN 100–320/MWh; 2026 76.1 TWh / PLN 24.9bn; non-price criteria); the NFOŚiGW scheme of PLN 4.15bn for 172 projects / 3.9 GW / 14.5 GWh plus Żarnowiec+Ełk 425 MW/2,032 MWh; the 2024-06-14 WDB reform, POB/DUB, PICASSO accession around July 2025 (grade B), MARI pending, and the TERRE exit on 2025-01-01; a negative price of −PLN 791.32/MWh on 2026-04-06 (grade C); the entry path for Chinese participants; ten pitfalls and a China–Poland comparison; a synthetic worked example (grade D).

Belgium and the Nordics electricity market: new Belgium/Nordics module (m-intl-benl, eighth in intl, 671 body lines). Belgium covers the single Belpex zone, 15-minute MTU and imbalance, CRM Y-4/Y-2/Y-1 (Y-4 cleared 4,690 MW, including 179 MW of new batteries / 525 MW nameplate, at a price in the ~€27k/MW·yr range but with the unit still to be verified (grade C); Y-2 at €25,100/MW·yr; Y-1 at a weighted ~€14,100/MW·yr), single-round sealed-bid pay-as-bid with an IPC, new build up to 15 years, Doel 4/Tihange 3 extended to 2035 and the May 2025 repeal of the phase-out law, offshore wind at 2.26 GW / 5.8 GW by 2030 / 8 GW by 2040, and 491 MWh of new storage in 2024; the Nordics cover 12 bidding zones (NO1–NO5, SE1–SE4, DK1–DK2, FI), Nord Pool system and zonal prices, the 15-minute MTU since 2025-10-01, 15-minute imbalance and mFRR EAM since 2025-03-04, the imbalance/day-ahead match falling from 33% to 3% and balancing costs rising from €1 to €5–6/MWh (grades B/C), PICASSO in Denmark (2024-10) and Finland (2025-03), Sweden's 800 MW effektreserv and its failed 2025-10-07 auction, Finland's tehoreservi, no capacity market in Norway/Denmark, negative prices and Danish offshore CfDs; the entry path for Chinese participants; ten pitfalls and comparisons; a synthetic worked example (grade D).

Covers MIBEL's two price zones (Spain and Portugal) inside EU coupling; OMIE day-ahead (12:00 CET gate) and intraday; the 15-minute MTU since 2025-10-01 and 15-minute imbalance settlement since 2024-12-01 (BOE-A-2025-5342); the two price bounds (−€600/+€4,000/MWh day-ahead vs. ±€9,999/MWh intraday); ~555 negative-price hours in 2025 and a €33.95/MWh solar capture price (grade C); the capacity market under Orden TED/966/2026 (BOE-A-2026-19329, in force 2026-09-18: peninsular firm power, pay-as-bid, new-build for up to 15 years, a 550 g CO2/kWh gate, first auction late 2026–2027); RD 997/2025 grid-forming and 120–130% voltage ride-through; RDL 7/2026 flexible access with a 10% self-consumption reserve; the PNIEC 22.5 GW storage target for 2030; the 2025-04-28 blackout background; the entry path for Chinese participants; ten pitfalls and a China–Spain comparison; a synthetic worked example (grade D).

Netherlands electricity market: new Netherlands module (m-intl-nl, sixth in intl, 580 body lines). Covers the single EPEX NL zone (separate from DE-LU); day-ahead and intraday; the 15-minute MTU since 2025-10-01 and 15-minute imbalance settlement; no capacity market (studied, not implemented); TenneT/ACM under the Energiewet in force 2026-01-01; SDE++ 2026 (€8bn, window 2026-10-27 to 2026-11-26, no standalone battery category); the end of net metering on 2027-01-01; aFRR dynamic dimensioning and mFRR asymmetric products from 1 MW; ATR85 non-firm contracts (~9 GW in 2025) and the priority framework from 2026-07-01; ~15,000 businesses waiting (grade C); 350 MW/620 MWh of storage at end-2024; the entry path for Chinese participants; ten pitfalls and a China–Netherlands comparison; a synthetic worked example (grade D).

Hub and atlas: the level-2 map adds "西班牙电力市场" and "荷兰电力市场" chips; atlas panel 08 becomes "Australia / Germany / UK / Italy / Spain / Netherlands market and storage design comparison" with six steps (Australia 5-minute, German FCR/aFRR/mFRR, UK T-4/T-1, Italian MACSE, Spain's 2026 rules, the Dutch no-capacity-market and congestion model); mini cards add the Spanish capacity market and the Dutch storage stack; fact blocks become 5 NEM regions / 7 Italian zones / 2 Iberian zones / 6 overseas modules; the caption explains that the six markets are not six versions of one rulebook and that storage revenue stacks differ even more.

Skills: the electricity-trading skill (both languages) expands §7A from four markets to six — a six-column market card, new "Spain: five must-knows" and "Netherlands: five must-knows", a six-market same-question table (7A.8), discipline (7A.9) covering EUR, the Iberian dual-zone design and Dutch congestion access, and reading paths (7A.10) for both modules; §15.4 now covers six markets and excludes Poland, Belgium and the Nordics. The storage skill (both languages) expands §14A to six markets, adds 14A.6 Spain, 14A.7 the Netherlands, the six-market comparison in 14A.8 and discipline in 14A.9; maintenance entry points and the quarterly review gain both modules.

Index and docs: INDEX_EN gains two module-map rows, eight overseas key-figure rows and two open items (#25 Spain, #26 the Netherlands); README / README_EN move to 53 modules / 21,540 body lines / 53 knowledge pages and add both countries to the overseas description and entry points; 更新清单 now audits 53 Markdown files (52 Chinese modules + 1 English index), with P1 growing from 16 to 18 items and the skill linkage and generated-artifact counts updated.

Sources and links: BOE (TED/966/2026, RDL 7/2026, 15-minute imbalance settlement), OMIE, CNMC, MITECO, ENTSO-E, RVO, ACM, EPEX Spot, Government.nl, CBS and Clean Energy Wire returned 200 and remain clickable; REE and TenneT return 403 to automated access and are shown as code text with the status noted; the Netbeheer Nederland domain is corrected to netbeheernederland.nl and returns 200; a JD Supra analysis of the Spanish capacity market returned 403 and is used only through search snippets, graded B and not linked; negative-price and storage-pipeline trend figures are grade C and not used for precise backtests.

entries.label: v1.9 maintenance: overseas expansion round 1 — the UK and Italy
items: Two new overseas modules: modules 49→51, body lines 18,914→20,344, Markdown files 72→74 (51 knowledge modules + 18 skill files + 5 repository-level documents). The intl order is now Australia's NEM (1), Germany (2), UK (3), Italy (4), Australia–Germany storage business (5, moved from 3); the section description and coverage in scripts/knowledge.config.mjs now cover four markets.

UK electricity market: new UK module (m-intl-uk, third in intl, 685 body lines). Covers the GB single market and the Northern Ireland boundary; NESO/Ofgem/Elexon roles; the EPEX GB hourly auction (10:20 CET gate) and GB-30min auction (16:30 CET gate); one-hour gate closure; half-hourly settlement and BSC reconciliation; pay-as-bid BM with BOALF (reported ~38% skip rate in 2026); capacity market T-4 2029/30 at £27.10/kW·yr for 40.1 GW and T-1 2026/27 at £5.00/kW·yr for 7,192 MW against a £75 cap and £49 net CONE; the CfD boundary for standalone storage; LDES cap and floor (minded-to 16 projects, 7,645 MW on 2026-06-26, final parameters autumn 2026); TMO4+ grid reform and REMA; TNUoS/DUoS/BSUoS; the storage revenue stack and the entry path for Chinese participants; ten pitfalls and a China–UK comparison; a synthetic worked example (grade D).

Italy electricity market: new Italy module (m-intl-it, fourth in intl, 733 body lines). Covers the seven mainland bidding zones (Nord, Centro-Nord, Centro-Sud, Sud, Calabria, Sicilia, Sardegna); GME's MGP (12:00 D-1 gate, SDAC-coupled, 15-minute MTU from 2025-10-01)/MI/MSD/MB/MTE; PUN as a reference price only; Terna's dual dispatch-and-procurement role; MACSE, the storage-specific 15-year pay-as-bid zonal auction (first round 10 GWh at an average €12,959/MWh·yr, 2028 delivery; second round 16 GWh on 2026-11-24, 2029 delivery; battery cap €37,000/MWh·yr); the capacity market and 2028 battery de-rating; FER X two-way CfD (DM 194/2026, 37.15 GW, 20 years, €80/MWh reference) and NZIA; connection queues and permitting; the entry path for Chinese participants; ten pitfalls and a China–Italy comparison; a synthetic worked example (grade D).

Hub and atlas: knowledge/index.template.html adds "英国电力市场" and "意大利电力市场" chips to the level-2 map; atlas panel 08 moves from two markets/5 steps to four markets/6 steps (Australia 5-minute, Germany 15-minute, German balancing, UK BM, UK T-4/T-1, Italian MACSE); mini cards add UK capacity prices, MACSE and the four-market storage revenue stacks; fact blocks now show 5 NEM regions, 7 Italian zones, the German 2031 capacity mechanism and 4 overseas modules; the caption explains the four different market designs and storage stacks. Three inline fixed-column overrides are removed in favour of .market-flow.six plus breakpoints, so the six-step flow becomes two columns below 960px and one below 620px, fixing the character-per-line overflow on mobile.

Skills: the electricity-trading skill (both languages) expands §7A from two markets to four — a four-column market card, new "UK GB: five must-knows" and "Italy: five must-knows", a four-market same-question table, discipline covering GBP/GB time/Italian zones/rule hierarchy, and reading paths for both modules; old 7A.5/7A.6 renumber to 7A.7/7A.8; §15.4 now covers four markets and excludes WA's WEM, the Northern Territory, Spain, the Netherlands, Poland and the Nordics. The storage skill (both languages) expands §14A to four markets, adds UK T-4/T-1, BM, LDES and MACSE revenue lines, and adds discipline such as "do not read MACSE €/MWh·yr as €/MW·yr" and "do not treat PUN as a settlement price"; maintenance entry points and quarterly review gain both modules.

Sources and links: both modules grade every source and note reachability; pages returning 200 (GOV.UK, Ofgem, UK REMIT, ARERA 247/2023/R/eel, EU SA.104106, Terna, Trade.gov, Review Energy, Modo, Solar Power Portal, Hill Dickinson, CNESA, Solarzoom) remain clickable; EPEX, NESO, Elexon, EMR, GME, MASE, GSE, Acquirente Unico, Argus and Solarbe returned 403/failed to automated access and are shown as code text with the status noted, not as clickable links.

entries.label: v1.9 maintenance: source verification and corrections for the overseas modules
items: German negative-price hours: 2024 corrected from 459 to 457 hours (BNetzA/SMARD); 2025's 573 hours upgraded from "media, grade B" to official grade A; 2023's 301 hours added. Noted that the 15-minute MTU from 2025-10 changes the counting basis, so year-on-year comparisons need care.

AgNes grid-fee timetable: corrected from "consultation 2026-08-06, decision by end-2026, effect 2029-01-01" to "process update 2026-05-27, draft determination 2026-10, final determination 2027-01-01, rules from 2029". Added the capacity-based charge of about €4–7/kW/year for utility-scale storage, existing storage applying after its §118(6) exemption expires, and the dynamic component from 2030 (storage) / 2032 (generation); BNetzA will not charge all storage from 2029-01-01.

German capacity-mechanism auctions: first auction 2026-09-08, second 2026-12-29, plus comprehensive auctions on 2027-10-31 and 2029-08-20; the two 2026 4.5 GW auctions are reportedly not open to battery storage, while the 2027 ~2 GW new-capacity tender is open to storage with ≥10 hours (grade B). The StromVKG "passed 2026-07" claim is softened to "provides the legal basis; passage and entry into force per the statute".

Australia IRP and reliability standard: IRP now states effective 2024-06-03; the 99.997% 2028–2032 reliability standard is now described as the Reliability Panel's April 2026 final-report recommendation rather than a draft; the AEMC IESS/IRP rule page is now a clickable link.

Australia–Germany storage module: WDRM direct-participation threshold changed from "about 1 MW" to "MW-scale (per AER guidance)"; §14a changed from a "4.2 kW threshold" to ">4.2 kW power threshold (LV connection)"; flexible export no longer claims Queensland and reads "DNSPs in South Australia, Victoria and other states"; capacity-market, AgNes and source tables mirror the corrections, with AEMC and BNetzA links now clickable.

Other checks: removed the unverified "€244k/MW/year" result column from the German capacity-auction table and replaced it with "results per the auction notice"; removed the unconfirmed "2026-07" month from the EEG 2027 draft amendment; marked the CIS Tender 9 and 10 results as "pending" in the watchlist.

Skills and docs: both language versions of the storage skill mirror the AgNes timetable, IRP effective date, ">4.2 kW" and capacity-market storage eligibility; README / INDEX_EN contained no repeated errors; body lines rise from 18,908 to 18,914, while the 49 modules and 72 Markdown files are unchanged.

entries.label: v1.9 maintenance: three overseas modules — Australia's NEM, Germany and Australia–Germany storage business
items: New section and structure: scripts/knowledge.config.mjs inserts an intl section (06 / GLOBAL, navigation label "海外市场") after spot and inter-provincial trading; the following eight sections renumber to 07 / PRICE … 14 / RESEARCH, and "method" becomes 15 / METHOD. Sections go from 10 to 11, modules from 46 to 49 and body lines from 16,745 to 18,908. The hub's level-2 map gains "澳大利亚 NEM", "德国电力市场" and "澳德储能业务" chips, its question becomes "how spot markets clear and settle, and how domestic and overseas markets connect", and the atlas grows to eight panels with an Australia/Germany market-and-storage design comparison.

Australia's NEM: new Australia NEM module (m-intl-au, first in intl, 713 body lines). Covers the five regions (Queensland, New South Wales, Victoria, South Australia, Tasmania; WA's WEM and the Northern Territory are out of scope), the AEMO/AEMC/AER split, energy-only dispatch co-optimised with FCAS, five-minute dispatch and settlement since 2021-10-01, NEM time fixed at AEST, the 2026-27 price bands (MPC A$23,200/MWh, CPT A$2,225,900/MWh, APC A$600/MWh, MFP −A$1,000/MWh, AFP −A$600/MWh), MLF/IRLF and settlement residues, RRO/RERT/CIS, LGC/SRES and IRP storage registration (IESS is the rule-change name, not a registration category), ASX contracts and PPAs, the entry path for Chinese participants, ten pitfalls, a China–Australia comparison and a synthetic worked example (grade D).

Germany: new Germany module (m-intl-de, second in intl, 716 body lines). Covers the DE-LU bidding zone inside EU coupling, EPEX day-ahead with a 12:00 CET gate and pay-as-clear, pay-as-bid intraday, the 15-minute MTU since 2025-10-01, the two different floors (SDAC −€500/MWh, SIDC −€9,999/MWh), FCR/aFRR/mFRR capacity and energy with PICASSO/MARI, Redispatch 2.0 since 2021-10-01 from 100 kW, EEG §51 zero value at negative prices and the repealed §60, §14a controllable loads, the AgNes grid-fee reform (draft determination 2026-10, final determination 2027-01-01, rules from 2029), the StromVKG capacity mechanism (from 2031, EU approval 2026-09-02), the entry path, ten pitfalls, a China–Germany comparison and a synthetic example (grade D).

Australia–Germany storage business: new storage business module (m-intl-storage, third in intl, 682 body lines), organised in four quadrants. Australian utility-scale covers arbitrage + FCAS + CIS, IRP/Generator/Market Customer registration and NSP connection plus MASS testing; Australian C&I covers demand charges, time-of-use spreads, CSIP-AUS flexible export and WDRM/VPP aggregation; German utility-scale covers EPEX 15-minute MTU, FCR/aFRR/mFRR, the §118(6) 20-year grid-fee exemption (commissioned by 2029-08-04), the AgNes 2029 reform and the StromVKG 2031 capacity mechanism; German C&I covers demand charges, the three §14a modules, dynamic tariffs and aggregation. Also includes an investment input contract, power/energy/time occupancy of the revenue stack, four synthetic worked examples (grade D), ten pitfalls, China–Australia and China–Germany comparisons and a 2026 watch list; the source table separates official texts, industry media and de-linked items.

Skill integration: both language versions of the electricity-trading skill add "7A. Overseas Markets Quick Reference (Australia NEM / Germany)" after §7, with a market-card table, five NEM points and formulas, six German points and formulas, a same-question comparison and answer discipline; §0.3 gains a knowledge-map row and §15.4 states the scope limit (NEM and DE-LU only, excluding WEM, the Northern Territory and the rest of Europe). Both language versions of the storage-investment skill add "14A. Overseas Quick Reference (Australia NEM / Germany DE-LU)" after §14, with four-quadrant market cards, five Australian points, six German points, a same-question comparison and six answer-discipline rules; §0.3, the maintenance entry points, sources and maintenance cadence gain overseas items. No tenth skill is added, to avoid duplicating the main trading and storage skills.

Accent and atlas: a low-saturation indigo accent (light #43548f / #e8ebf6, dark #a3b2e8 / #1c2440) is wired through data-cat="intl" on the hub and body[data-cat="intl"] on reading pages; the eighth atlas panel uses a five-step flow, three mini cards (the third is "storage four quadrants") and four fact blocks, with a caption stating that the two markets are not two versions of one rulebook and that storage revenue structures differ even more.

Docs and calibres: README / README_EN, INDEX_EN, this file and 更新清单 all move to 49 modules / 18,908 body lines / 72 Markdown files (49 knowledge modules + 18 skill files + 5 repository-level documents); the English index adds the three module rows, an overseas key-figures table and a 22nd open item. All three modules carry a 2026-11-01 cutoff, every price band states its time point and scope, and all worked examples are synthetic (grade D), not investment advice.

Mobile anchor landing: opening a #section deep link used to smooth-scroll from the top for about 1.5 seconds before settling, and after fonts loaded the active nav item could still sit on the previous section. Initial hash landings are now instant, smooth scrolling resumes afterwards, sticky-offset recalculation refreshes the active item, and every activation pass re-scrolls the horizontal nav so the active pill ("06 海外市场") stays fully visible. Click-to-scroll navigation remains smooth.

Checks: build, --check and the consistency check pass; 49 knowledge pages + 18 skill pages + 18 TXT files are rebuilt; new external links were tested and kept only where the official page loaded (AEMO/AEMC/AER/regelleistung block automated access, which the modules note; only the EnWG §14a and §118(6) pages remain clickable); desktop and mobile screenshots cover the new section, cards, atlas panel and all three reading pages.

entries.label: v1.9 maintenance: full UI/UX pass on the knowledge base
items: Filters, anchors and empty state: in-page anchors inside cards hidden by a filter no longer jump into empty space — clicking a same-page anchor clears the filter before scrolling; an empty result offers a "clear filters" button and explains why; filter and search state is written to ?q=&type= and restored on reload or from a shared link. Search is debounced at 150ms, adds a clear button (32px desktop, 40px mobile), highlights through a TreeWalker limited to text nodes, clears on Escape, announces the result count via aria-live, and filter buttons expose aria-pressed.

Mobile sticky offsets: the sidebar height feeds --hub-header and --hub-scroll-offset (sidebar + filter bar + 16px), recomputed on resize, font load and ResizeObserver callbacks; html{scroll-padding-top} now owns anchor landing. Reading pages drop the doubled scroll-margin-top on headings and keep --topbar-h + 18px.

Whole-card targets: the module-card title link stretches across the card, leaving one tab stop per card; the overlay carries z-index:1 so the card bottom is clickable too, and keyboard focus shows a card-level ring.

Mobile filter bar and tap targets: below 760px the filter buttons collapse into a native select, the result count is visually hidden but stays in aria-live, and tap heights for hub navigation, buttons, clear controls and the reading page's back, TOC, source, theme and policy chips settle at 40–44px; back-to-top grows from 34px to 44px and stays available on mobile.

Reading-page drawer: opening the TOC locks background scrolling and sets inert on .main/.toc; Tab cycles inside the drawer, Escape, the scrim or any entry closes it and returns focus to the trigger, and viewports at 901px or wider close it automatically.

Contrast and type: amber #8a5410, green #37703f, teal #0d6a63, VPP #8a5a12 and slate #5a6470 replace the lighter accents; control borders deepen to #7f8a91 (dark #66737e) for 3:1, and every text pair passes WCAG AA in both themes. --fs-read:15.5px becomes the reading body and lede size, folding a dozen scattered 10–13.8px values into the seven-step --fs-2xs…--fs-lg scale; white cards gain --card-line borders and --shadow-card to separate them from the canvas; the reading measure narrows from 43rem to 39rem.

Sidebar note: the "阅读原则" block in the bottom-left corner changes from a single 11px line hugging the edge into a bordered, rounded light-grey card — a monospaced kicker with a short rule, three principles on separate dotted lines at 12.5px; desktop viewports 820px or shorter also tighten nav spacing and card padding so all 15 sections fit at 1366×768 without scrolling.

Code and artifacts: new knowledge/assets/tokens.css centralises colour, font and type tokens, inlined into the hub at build time and linked by reading pages, removing two duplicate theme token blocks; the table first column is no longer forced to nowrap, using min-width:6.5em on mobile while keeping horizontal scroll; prefers-reduced-motion is honoured; the unused visible map in the IntersectionObserver is gone; the progress bar updates aria-valuenow live; the module-card CTA changes from ↗ to "进入模块 →" (policy external links keep ↗); the hub stops publishing internal "XX 行" metadata; and the hero panel below 1180px switches from hidden to a compact two-column layout.

Checks: 46 modules / 16,745 lines / 69 Markdown files and the artifact counts are unchanged; build, --check and the consistency check pass; screenshots were reviewed at a 390×844 viewport and on desktop in light and dark mode, with scripted checks for filter/anchor behaviour, search debounce/highlight/URL restore, whole-card clicks, the drawer focus trap, progress semantics and the contrast matrix.

items: White light theme: the light tokens for the hub and reading pages change from paper-yellow to pure white — --paper from #f6f2e9 to #fff and --card from #fffdf8 to #fff; the secondary surface --paper-2 becomes a neutral light grey #f4f6f7 for tags, counts and table headers. entries.label: v1.9 maintenance: two-tone identity — pale-teal book, dark-teal bolt
items: Two-tone mark: knowledge/assets/logo-book.svg moves from a single monochrome silhouette to two paths: the book is filled pale teal #dcefe9 and outlined with a 3.2-wide, 35%-opaque dark-teal stroke; the bolt becomes a solid #0e6b66 shape on top instead of a cutout.
